blocks.title: The Parent Cube Root Function

discoveryHook.scenario: Unlike a square root, you CAN take the cube root of a negative number! The graph goes left and right, up and down — it lives in all four quadrants. This S‑shaped curve is the parent of all cube root functions.

Cube root functions transform just like square root functions! The general form $y = a\sqrt[3]{x-h} + k$ lets you shift the S‑curve left/right and up/down, stretch or shrink it, and even flip it over. The point $(h,k)$ is the new 'center' of the graph.

formulaCard.title: General Cube Root Function
notes: Domain and range: all real numbers.

explanation: General form: $y = a\sqrt[3]{x - h} + k$. The graph's 'center' (inflection point) is at $(h, k)$.
Horizontal shift: $h>0$ right, $h<0$ left (opposite the sign).
Vertical shift: $k>0$ up, $k<0$ down.
Reflection: If $a<0$, the graph flips vertically (decreasing instead of increasing).
Stretch/Shrink: $|a|>1$ steeper; $0<|a|<1$ flatter.

confusionCorner.title: Inside vs. Outside
confusionCorner.body: Changes inside the radical ($x-h$) move left/right but [[imp:opposite]] the sign. Changes outside ($+k$) move up/down exactly as they appear. $a$ changes steepness; negative $a$ flips.

confusionCorner.title: Use the Same Interval!
confusionCorner.body: To compare growth rates fairly, always use the [[imp:same x-interval]] for both functions. Different intervals give different average rates even for the same function.

explanation: The [[kw:average rate of change]] between $a$ and $b$ is $\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$.
For cube root functions, the rate decreases as $|x|$ gets large — the graph flattens out.
To compare two functions, compute the average rate over the SAME interval.
A steeper graph has a larger average rate of change.
Example: $m(x)$ from graph: $(0,0)$ to $(8,8)$ → avg rate $= 8/8 = 1$. $h(x) = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{4}x}$: $(0,0)$ to $(8,\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.3)$ → avg rate $= 1.3/8 \approx 0.16$.
